case_title: N. Parameswaran Unni v. G. Kannan and Another
accused_victim_relationship: Creditor-debtor: the accused borrowed money from the complainant
statutory_provisions: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 s.138 r/w s.142
evidence_type: Documentary: cheques, bank intimation memo, legal notices and postal endorsements
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.138 NI Act; sentenced to three months simple imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Revision allowed; concurrent conviction set aside on ground that the demand notice was beyond 15 days
offence_finally_established: Dishonour of cheque under s.138 NI Act (r/w s.142); sentence replaced by payment in lieu of imprisonment
neutral_facts: The accused borrowed Rs. 64,000 from the complainant in October 1990. In repayment the accused issued two cheques dated 13 October 1990 for Rs. 10,000 and Rs. 25,000, drawn on a bank at Alappuzha, and a third cheque for Rs. 29,000 dated 08 October 1990, drawn on a different bank and issued by a third person. The complainant presented the first two cheques to his bank in April 1991. The accused's bank returned them on 05 April 1991 with the endorsement 'Refer to drawer', and the complainant's bank intimated the dishonour on 08 April 1991. The complainant issued a legal notice on 12 April 1991 demanding payment. The postal endorsement read 'intimation served, addressee absent' and the notice was received back by the complainant's advocate on 25 April 1991. A second notice was sent on 04 May 1991 and was returned with the endorsement 'Refused, returned to sender'. The complainant alleged that the accused had not repaid the borrowed amount and that the cheques were dishonoured for insufficiency of funds. The documentary evidence comprised the cheques, the bank memos, the legal notices and the postal endorsements.
offence_severity: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine up to twice the cheque amount, or both; no minimum stated
financial_property_loss: Rs. 64,000 (loan amount underlying the dishonoured cheques)
motive: alleged: failure to repay the loan of Rs. 64,000
key_evidence_accepted: Cheques, bank intimation memo and first legal notice dated 12.04.1991 with postal endorsement; first notice held deemed served
bail_history: Not stated in detail; judgment refers only to bail granted to the first respondent, to be cancelled if the deposit is not made
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: 29-07-1993; High Court: 06-10-2003; Supreme Court: March 2017 (from header only)
legal_representation: Accused (respondents): C. K. Sasi, Manu Krishnan G., Abraham Mathews (for P. V. Dinesh). Appellant (complainant): M. Gireesh Kumar, Sriram P., Ms. Athira G. Nair (for Ankur S. Kulkarni). No State counsel; the State is not a party.
investigation_status: Private complaint lodged on 23.05.1991; no police investigation mentioned; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted, three months simple imprisonment (29-07-1993). Appellate court (Addl. Sessions Judge): appeal dismissed (07-07-1995). High Court: revision allowed, conviction set aside (06-10-2003). Supreme Court: High Court judgment set aside; conviction restored with sentence replaced by deposit of Rs. 2,00,000.
prosecution_argument: Not separately recorded; the appellant's position was that the first notice was validly served and the complaint was filed within time
defence_argument: Not separately recorded beyond the High Court ground that the demand notice was beyond 15 days; counsel offered Rs. 2,00,000 in lieu of imprisonment
legal_principle_applied: Notice sent by registered post to the correct address is deemed served under s.27 General Clauses Act and s.114 Evidence Act, rebuttable by the drawer; a reminder notice does not negate the first notice; complaint filed within s.142(b) time
precedent_relied_upon: M/s New India Sugar Mills Ltd. v. Commissioner of Sales Tax, AIR 1963 SC 1207; Jagdish Singh v. Natthu Singh, (1992) 1 SCC 647; State of M.P. v. Hiralal, (1996) 7 SCC 523; V. Raja Kumari v. P. Subbarama Naidu, (2004) 8 SCC 774
sentencing_rationale: Not applicable as a reasoned sentence; on counsel's undertaking the sentence was replaced by payment of Rs. 2,00,000 in lieu of three months' simple imprisonment, with no separate reasoning given
other_sentence_order: Accused to deposit Rs. 2,00,000 before JFCM-II, Alappuzha by 30.04.2017; Rs. 1,30,000 of it paid to the complainant as compensation; if not deposited, the three-month sentence is restored and bail cancelled
